title: Object of praedestinatio — parallel opinion-splits in both Schools
source_text: XXXII. Quemadmodum autem Theologi tum Ecclesiae Romanae, tum Ecclesiae Reformatae, de effectis electionis & praedestinationis varie philosophantur, sic apud utrosque judicia variant, nec parva reperitur opinionum diversitas circa praedestinationis & electionis objectum, id est, quum quaeritur sub qua ratione, & quo respectu homo praedestinanti Deo objiciatur. Eademque propemodum sententiarum discrimina quae inveniuntur in Schola Reformata, in Schola quoque Romana locum habent. Ut apparere potest repetenti quae supra dicta sunt.
pass_a_gloss: But just as Theologians both of the Roman Church and of the Reformed Church philosophize variously concerning the effects of election and predestination, so among both judgments vary, and no small diversity of opinions is found concerning the object of predestination and election — that is, when it is asked under what reason and in what respect man is set before God predestining. And nearly the same discriminations of opinions which are found in the Reformed School have place also in the Roman School. As can appear to one who repeats what has been said above.
pass_b_english: Effect-disputes and object-disputes travel together in both Schools.
Question: under what ratio/respect is man object to God predestining?
Nearly the same opinion-splits in Reformed and Roman Schools.
